transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-02-14 16:30 PST
Duration: ~55 minutes
Location: Zoom
Attendees: Alex Chen (Redwood AE), Maya Rodriguez (Redwood SE), Samir Patel (Redwood SE), Lena Ortiz (Skybound - Head of ML), Tom Harrell (Skybound - Platform), Jared Kim (Skybound - CTO), Priya Rao (Skybound - Data Scientist)

Auto-summary (auto-generated, may be incomplete):
- Goal: scope POC for model serving with reserved GPUs + burst strategy + fallback policies.
- Success criteria discussed: p50/p95 latency SLO, throughput targets, cost per 1k tokens, functional quality baseline.
- Workload: mixture of short chat-like queries (avg 40 tokens) + long completion jobs (avg 512 tokens).
- Next: Redwood to run benchmarks on reserved pool, customer to share traces/dataset, follow-up to agree commit.

Topics covered:
- POC success metrics (latency SLOs, throughput, quality regressions)
- Sizing reserved pool for pilot (GPU types, instance counts)
- Burst strategy and fallback rules (quantized variants, smaller models, cross-region fallback)
- Benchmark design (prefix/cache, KV cache warmup, synthetic vs real traces)
- Timeline and commercial/contractal items

Transcript body:
[00:00] Alex Chen: hey everyone thanks for joining, we'll try to keep to 45-60, um the goal here is to scope the pilot sizing and autoscale so we get you a clean benchmark and a recommended reserve size.
[00:21] Lena Ortiz: cool thanks, yes we're trying to prove performance for our assistant feature, we want p50 under 120ms for short queries and p95 < 800ms for longer completions, that's our target.
[00:35] Tom Harrell: to add, primary constraints are cost — we can't oversubscribe GPUs — and also data residency, we need the test in us-west but also eventually in eu-west.
[00:50] Maya Rodriguez: got it. quick question on workload mix — do you have a percent split between short qps and long completions?
[00:57] Priya Rao: right now it's approx 70% short (40 tokens avg), 30% long (350-600 tokens), but there are daily spikes during batch runs.
[01:12] Samir Patel: ok that mix matters for batching and KV cache hit rates. for the POC we usually run two benchmark passes: one simulating production traces (your 1k trace) and one synthetic steady-state to push throughput.
[01:29] Jared Kim: how many GPUs are we talking for the reserved pool? we want predictable latency but avoid wasted spend.
[01:36] Alex Chen: preliminary ballpark — for a pilot of 500 qps sustained with your mix, conservatively you'd need a reserved pool equivalent to ~6-8 A10G-class GPUs depending on quantization and batch strategy. if you go fp16 and enable prefix caching we often drop that 20-30%.
[01:58] Tom Harrell: hmm A10G — we're on GCP with T4s today. switching to A10G for the POC is fine but we need a cost estimate.
[02:08] Maya Rodriguez: we'll include cost table, but important to note reserved capacity gives predictable latency and reserved pricing; burst can sit on shared capacity up to x rps but with different SLOs.
[02:22] Lena Ortiz: can you explain the burst and fallback flow? what happens when reserved pool saturates?
[02:27] Samir Patel: yes so typical pattern we recommend: primary -> reserved pool (pinned GPUs) for production traffic; when utilization hits threshold (e.g., 85%) route overflow to burst capacity in hosted pool; if hosted pool is also constrained, fallback rules kick in: serve using quantized smaller model (e.g., 8-bit LLM variant) or degrade max tokens, or fall back to a cached response for repeat requests.
[02:52] Priya Rao: do you support automatic model variant fallbacks? like auto-switch to 8-bit if latency spikes?
[02:58] Maya Rodriguez: yes, Redwood has routing policies that can do model variant swap with canary windows and A/B style rollouts — for the POC we'll test automatic fallback to a lower-precision variant with strict monitoring.
[03:14] Alex Chen: quick note — prefix caching and KV cache warmup are critical. for your chat use-case the first few cold requests will be slower until KV warms; benchmarks should include a cold-to-warm phase.
[03:28] Lena Ortiz: we absolutely need KV cache warmup in the benchmark; otherwise numbers will look bad. also want to measure cost per 1k tokens.
[03:37] Tom Harrell: on the fallback to smaller model, what's the quality delta? can we get evals before we enable that permanently?
[03:44] Samir Patel: yes we'll produce side-by-side evals on your prompt set — Redwood Optimize recommendations will include quantization profile and quality regression numbers. we'll annotate any deltas so you can decide acceptable thresholds.
[03:58] Jared Kim: timeline — how long to run the benchmark and provide results?
[04:02] Alex Chen: we can kick the benchmark within 2 business days after we get the trace and sample data, runs typically take 3-4 days including ablation, then we'll share a report. so expect report in ~1 week.
[04:16] Priya Rao: sounds good. do you need any infra changes from our side for private VPC or just for hosted?
[04:22] Maya Rodriguez: for the POC we'll run on Redwood Dedicated in your preferred region; minimal changes — just credentials to a temporary S3 share and optional VPC peering if you want network isolation. we'll provide a checklist.
[04:35] Tom Harrell: about autoscaling policies — can we set different thresholds for short and long requests?
[04:41] Samir Patel: you can configure route-level policies; i.e., route /chat to a low-latency profile with tighter autoscale, and /batch to a throughput profile with larger batch sizes. for the POC we'll propose two route configs and test both.
[04:58] Lena Ortiz: cost modeling — can you model cost both for reserved only and reserved+burst? we need to compare committed spend vs hybrid.
[05:05] Alex Chen: yes we'll include three scenarios: reserved only (no burst), reserved + managed burst (mixed), and aggressive quantized fallback (cheaper but lower quality). we'll include per-1k token cost and projected monthly spend at 100k qpm.
[05:22] Jared Kim: security checklist — SOC2, SSO, KMS?
[05:25] Maya Rodriguez: yes we have SOC 2 Type II, SAML SSO integrations, and KMS support for key management. for private deployments we can support HSM if needed.
[05:36] Tom Harrell: any caveats about cross-region fallback? if eu-west goes down can we run in us-west?
[05:42] Samir Patel: we support cross-region fallback, but note data residency and latency impacts — you'll need to sign off on that. for the POC we'll keep tests in us-west and a controlled eu-west run later.
[05:55] Speaker 2: (inaudible) i had a question about the benchmark metrics — do you measure token-level latency or end-to-end application latency?
[06:03] Maya Rodriguez: both. we'll provide per-token compute time, model latency, network e2e latency, and application-level p50/p95. and we'll break down cost by token compute vs network.
[06:20] Priya Rao: one more — can the benchmark simulate sudden spikes e.g., 3x for 5 minutes?
[06:25] Samir Patel: yes we include spike tests. we'll test ramp, sustained, and spike patterns and show how routing/fallback kicks in at each level.
[06:34] Lena Ortiz: ok good. for success criteria: p50 < 120ms for short, p95 < 800ms for long, cost < $0.50 per 1k tokens for the pilot baseline, and no quality regressions > 2% on our eval set.
[06:49] Alex Chen: noted. we'll calibrate benchmark to show those metrics.
[06:53] Tom Harrell: are there common gotchas?
[06:55] Samir Patel: a couple — 1) underestimating cold-starts / KV warmup, 2) not accounting for batch sizing variation across seq lengths, 3) overlooking prefix caching effectiveness. we'll instrument each.
[07:09] Alex Chen: ok let's recap next steps — Redwood runs bench, customer provides traces/data, follow up to review.
[07:16] Jared Kim: sounds good, please include committed pricing for 1 and 3 month pilots — and the POC contract.
[07:22] Alex Chen: we will.
[07:24] Lena Ortiz: thanks everyone.
[07:26] End of meeting.
